summary: Russia launched a massive overnight drone attack with 155 Shahed-type UAVs, of which 110 were destroyed or suppressed, while Ukrainian forces struck the Marinovka airfield in Russia's Volgograd region with Neptune missiles. Russian Geran-5 missiles targeted Kyiv's Desnyansky district and a thermal power plant, and Russian forces advanced near Petropavlivka on the eastern front. North Korea temporarily halted missile supplies to Russia, and EU financial aid for Ukraine faces blockage from four member states.
key_points: Russia launched 155 Shahed drones overnight; Ukrainian air defense destroyed or suppressed 110, with impacts recorded at 27 locations. (Source: @kpszsu/99633)
Ukrainian Navy struck Marinovka airfield in Volgograd region with Neptune missiles, targeting Su-34 bombers that drop glide bombs. (Source: @UkraineNow/85553)
Russian Geran-5 missiles hit Kyiv's Desnyansky district and a thermal power plant, causing fires and damage. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78795)
Russian forces advanced near Petropavlivka in the eastern front sector. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24030)
North Korea temporarily suspended missile and artillery shipments to Russia after Russian deputy FM remarks. (Source: @UkraineNow/85549)
Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary, and Bulgaria block €45 billion EU aid package for Ukraine in 2027 over repayment conditions. (Source: @UkraineNow/85555)
Crimea and Sevastopol suffered a massive blackout due to a power grid failure outside the peninsula. (Source: @UkraineNow/85558)
Ukrainian strike destroyed a Russian accumulation point in central Huliaipole used for offensive operations. (Source: @UkraineNow/85561)

sections.executive_summary: Russia launched a massive overnight drone attack with 155 Shahed-type UAVs, of which 110 were destroyed or suppressed, while Ukrainian forces struck the Marinovka airfield in Russia's Volgograd region with Neptune missiles. Russian Geran-5 missiles targeted Kyiv's Desnyansky district and a thermal power plant, and Russian forces advanced near Petropavlivka on the eastern front. North Korea temporarily halted missile supplies to Russia, and EU financial aid for Ukraine faces blockage from four member states.

points: Ukrainian air defense destroyed or suppressed 110 of 155 Shahed-type drones launched overnight from multiple Russian directions including Orel, Millerovo, Kursk, Shatalovo, Primorsko-Akhtarsk, occupied Donetsk, and occupied Crimea. (Source: @kpszsu/99633)

Ukrainian Navy coastal missile forces struck the Marinovka airfield in Russia's Volgograd region with Neptune missiles; the base hosts Su-34 fighter-bombers that launch glide bombs against Ukrainian cities and positions. (Source: @UkraineNow/85553)

Ukrainian aviation destroyed a Russian personnel accumulation point in central Huliaipole, Zaporizhzhia region, which served as a gathering point for further offensive actions. (Source: @UkraineNow/85561)

Starlink and Starshield connectivity restored on Ukrainian-controlled territory but restrictions persist in occupied areas; President Zelenskyy stated the decision involves both SpaceX technical and political dimensions. (Source: @UkraineNow/85569)
Ukraine received bodies of 250 fallen servicemen from Russia; the Russian side confirmed they belong to Ukrainian military personnel. (Source: @UkraineNow/85563)
Cabinet of Ministers ordered verification of data for all men aged 17 to 60 to update the Unified State Register of conscripts, military obligates, and reservists. (Source: @UkraineNow/85562)
Ukraine received $450 million from the World Bank with Japanese support via RISE and SURGE programs, supporting small businesses and reconstruction planning. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24028)

Russia launched 155 attack drones (83 jet-powered Shaheds, plus Gerber and Parodiya decoys) from Orel, Millerovo, Kursk, Shatalovo, Primorsko-Akhtarsk, occupied Donetsk, and occupied Crimea (Gvardeyskoye). (Source: @kpszsu/99633)

Russian forces fired Geran-5 missiles at Kyiv's Desnyansky district and a thermal power plant, with at least two missiles tracked from Kyiv region toward Zhytomyr region's Korosten district. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78795)
A third Tu-160 strategic bomber relocated from the Far East to Engels airbase for cruise missile loading, indicating preparation for future strikes. (Source: @eRadarrua/133402)
Crimea and Sevastopol experienced a complete blackout during daytime on November 26 due to a power grid accident outside the peninsula; restoration timelines unknown. (Source: @UkraineNow/85558)

Salekhard in Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug suffered a massive blackout affecting ~50,000 residents due to ice accumulation on power lines; heating, water, and electricity cut off. (Source: @eRadarrua/133405)

Russian air defense claimed 45 drones shot down over Leningrad region overnight; falling debris hit a residential high-rise and the Yefremov synthetic rubber plant in Tula region. (Source: @UkraineNow/85565)

North Korea temporarily halted missile and artillery supplies to Russia following Russian deputy foreign minister's statement about reducing tensions with South Korea; decision reportedly made by Kim Jong Un. (Source: @UkraineNow/85549)
Russian forces advanced near Petropavlivka in the eastern front sector, according to updated frontline mapping. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24030)
Ukrainian strike eliminated a Russian troop accumulation point in central Huliaipole, Zaporizhzhia region, disrupting offensive preparations. (Source: @UkraineNow/85561)

sections.threat_assessment: The scale of the overnight drone attack (155 UAVs) demonstrates Russia's sustained capacity for massed aerial strikes despite Ukrainian air defense effectiveness. The use of Geran-5 missiles against Kyiv indicates continued integration of newer missile types into strike packages. Ukrainian strikes on Russian airbases (Marinovka, Engels Tu-160 deployment) show growing long-range strike capability targeting the launch platforms for glide bombs. Frontline movement near Petropavlivka suggests Russian offensive pressure persists in the east. North Korea's supply pause may temporarily reduce Russian artillery and missile stocks but could resume pending diplomatic shifts.
sections.regional_response: EU unity on Ukraine funding is fracturing: four member states block the €45 billion 2027 package, while Germany conditions its budget approval on unanimous participation. Czech President Pavel's public disagreement with PM Babiš highlights domestic political divisions. Armenia's move to replace Russian border guards with its own forces signals a strategic pivot away from Russian security guarantees in the South Caucasus. Japan's $450 million World Bank contribution via RISE/SURGE programs underscores continued G7 financial support.
sections.intelligence_notes: Starlink/Starshield restoration on Ukrainian-held territory but not in occupied areas suggests SpaceX maintains geofencing controls, with Zelenskyy attributing the decision to both technical and political factors. The third Tu-160 deployment to Engels indicates Russia is regenerating its strategic bomber force for potential large-scale missile strikes. Winter weather arrival (snow across multiple regions) will affect ground mobility and drone operations. The Salekhard and Crimea blackouts reveal vulnerabilities in Russian energy infrastructure far from the front lines.
